coaching.title: B2B Day 2 — 6 mi + 700 ft
coaching.message: Calendar says back-to-back day 2 on legs that just absorbed 24 mi and 3,800 ft. Six miles, roughly 700 ft, strictly Zone 2 (138-150 bpm) — and if the first mile feels ugly, walk it. The point today is not fitness, it's durability: teaching your legs to move well when they are already emptied, which is exactly mile 38 of the Julian Alps. Run the descents relaxed and light-footed rather than braking; quads that stay quiet on tired downhills are what carry you off Vršič. Cap it at 6 miles even if you feel good — this was the last big block, 25 days out, and taper starts now.

coaching.title: Refill Before You Run
coaching.message: You went out fully fueled yesterday, so glycogen is low this morning. Take 40-60g of fast carbs before you head out (toast + honey, banana, or a gel) rather than running this one fasted — the goal is quality movement, not more depletion. It's short enough to skip mid-run fuel, but carry 500ml with 500-700mg sodium; Cieneguilla is dry and warm. Then hit the 30-minute window hard: 30-40g protein plus 80-100g carbs. Total carb target today sits near the training number, not the 220g rest-day floor — you're still paying back two days of work.

coaching.title: Close the Block Properly
coaching.message: This closes your peak block, so treat this afternoon as recovery, not filler. Legs elevated for 15 minutes after the run, then easy quad, calf, and hip flexor mobility — no aggressive foam rolling on eccentrically trashed quads today, keep it light. You have the Steelman Clinic appointment at 2:15 and dinner at 5:30; walk between them rather than sitting the whole gap. Sleep target 8+ hours tonight. The 3,800 ft of descent from yesterday is still repairing, and that repair is the training adaptation.

coaching.title: The Work Is Banked
coaching.message: Twenty-five days out — this morning's 6 miles is the last rep of the hardest block you'll do for this race. From here the job flips from building to protecting. Expect the taper itch: you'll feel undertrained, twitchy, convinced you should add one more long day. You shouldn't. Every mile from now is a deposit you don't spend until Kranjska Gora. Notice how you feel running on empty this morning — bookmark it. That exact sensation, handled calmly, is what race day asks of you.
